content:
tara_support: fyi, acme just opened a ticket — Dedicated pool `acme-prod` saw sustained TPS spike and we're returning 429s + token-per-second SLO violations. customer reports higher bill too. logs attached below.

june_acme: seeing ~2500 tps for ~2m, then 429s. we didn't change workload. observed lots of 401 retries too. billing alarm triggered: unexpected token delta.

metrics-bot: Metric alert: dedicated/acme-prod/tps 2.5k (>SLO 2k) at 2026-03-17T12:15Z; burst_credits remaining: 0

devon_sre: looking. can you paste a sample request id and time? also any token refresh logs?

june_acme: req: req_20260317_121501 id. sample curl: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"gpt-neox-20b"}'`

tara_support: copied logs: 
```
2026-03-17T12:14:58Z ERROR 401 refresh_token failed for client acme-client-2: invalid_grant
2026-03-17T12:15:01Z WARN admission_control: admit=false reason=burst_credits_exhausted pool=acme-prod
2026-03-17T12:15:02Z ERROR 429 request=req_20260317_121501 reason=admission_reject
```

devon_sre: hunch: simultaneous auth failures caused retry storm, which depleted burst credits; also seeing a heavy embedding job from pod embedder-12 at same time (large batch size=8192) causing long GPU loops -> noisy neighbor. checking autoscaler logs.

oncall-bot: Deploy detected: autoscaler v2.3.1 applied 2026-03-17T11:55Z -> config `scale_cooldown=120s`.

leo_prod: autoscaler cooldown might be too long for short spikes; admission controller uses instantaneous headroom calc that assumes cooldown 30s. mismatch can cause underprovisioning during bursts.

devon_sre: action items: 1) throttle/limit embedder-12 batch sizes; 2) temporarily bump burst_credits for acme-prod by +30% to recover; 3) patch autoscaler to use moving average window; 4) investigate billing token double-count.

tara_support: june_acme ok to apply emergency changes? they prefer minimal disruptions.

june_acme: yes please, prioritise recovery. we can pause the large embed job if needed.

devon_sre: implementing: `kubectl exec -it embedder-12 -- bash -c "export BATCH_SIZE=1024 && pkill -USR1 -f run_embed.sh"`

oncall-bot: Burst credits update: pool=acme-prod delta=+30% applied by devon (temp) at 2026-03-17T12:19Z

metrics-bot: admission_control rejects dropped from 1200/min -> 40/min after changes. TPS stabilized to 1.9k by 12:22Z

leo_prod: follow-ups: add a guard in auth client to avoid synchronized token refresh (jitter), add billing reconciliation job to detect token-count anomalies, and add headroom buffer config to Dedicated pools (+20%).

devon_sre: repro instructions for runbook: 
1) run a 2.5k tps synthetic load against pool with simultaneous token-refresh spike. tool: `wrk -t8 -c500 -d120s --script=burst.lua http://...`
2) submit a large-embedding batch (>=8k tokens) from a single pod to simulate noisy neighbor
3) observe burst_credits, admission rejects, and billing spikes

tara_support: i've updated the ticket with runbook and customer's permission. closing as active-ops. will ping when billing team confirms token counts.

billing-bot: Billing alert: preliminary check shows tokens counted correctly but two retry spikes inflated billable completions. Recommend credits refund for period 12:14-12:20Z.

june_acme: thanks all. appreciate quick fix :thumbsup: 

devon_sre: leaving follow-up RFC to prod/infra: autoscaler window + admission headroom + jittered auth refresh. assigning to leo.

leo_prod: acknowledged. will draft RFC by EOD.
